text:
Lena: Alerting here — SFO1 region is reporting control-plane + data-plane instability across multiple clusters. Grafana: API 5xx spike, node-heartbeat missing. Seeing large number of GPU nodes flip to ProvisioningFailed. Paging oncall.
ops-bot: [ALERT] SFO1: cluster-api-errors > threshold (last 2m). Incident created: auto-1778250001. @oncall-team
Mike: Confirming from the cluster side — kubernetes API returning 503s, autoscaler can't place pods, pods stuck in Pending with 'insufficient' errors. Sample: ```kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME               STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-01        NotReady   gpu      6d    v1.27.3
gpu-node-02        NotReady   gpu      6d    v1.27.3
control-plane-01   Unknown    master   7d    v1.27.3
```
Ashley: I can see BGP withdraws for SFO1 from provider telemetry — routes to some AZs are being blackholed intermittently. Provider status: https://status.cloudprovider.example/sfo1 (networking incident).
Jordan: Starting traffic shift to us-west2 now. Will do staged weights: 25% -> 50% -> 100% unless backend errors increase. Command: `redwood route update --from-region sfo1 --to-region us-west2 --weight 50`
Lena: @Mike you're primary oncall. Please open provider case, collect node serials and attach kubelet/journal logs. Notify customer-facing comms team. :rotating_light:
Mike: Opening case with provider — INC-5773. Uploaded node IDs, cluster logs, and control-plane traces. Provider acknowledged; assigned to network-eng. Initial note: possible routing flap from vendor SW update.
netops-bot: Runbook triggered: `multi-region-failover-v2` — checklist pushed to incident page. Links: https://runbooks.redwood/multi-region-failover
Ashley: Pausing cache invalidations and any global KV writes — we may have stale KV replicas in SFO1 that will diverge during failover.
Jordan: FYI — shifting traffic will cause egress and cross-region replication charges to spike. Noted for finance: tagging incident for cost tracking. :money_with_wings:
Mike: Trying a manual restart of kubelet on NotReady nodes to see if we can restore heartbeat while provider works on networking: `gcloud compute ssh gpu-node-01 -- sudo systemctl restart kubelet` — will post results shortly.
Lena: Quick plan: 1) Continue stepwise traffic shift to us-west2 and monitor error rates. 2) Work with provider for network rollback. 3) Collect all logs, core dumps, and attach to INC-5773. 4) Draft customer status update: short, factual, and point to mitigation (traffic routing).
Ashley: Paste of head of kubelet logs showing flaps: ```Mar 18 14:03:21 gpu-node-01 kubelet[1234]: E0318 14:03:21.123 kubelet_node_status.go:89] Couldn't register node: failed to get node lease: context deadline exceeded
Mar 18 14:03:24 gpu-node-01 kubelet[1234]: NodeNotReady: network unreachable
```
cloud-provider: We've escalated to network team — evidence of routing instability after a software deployment in SFO exchange. We're rolling back that change now and tracking progress with ENG-NET-2. ETA not yet confirmed.
Mike: Setting incident severity to Sev1. Incident page created: https://incidents.redwood/1778250001. Notifying Customer Success for comms.
Jordan: Monitoring metrics: request latency stable at 1.2s after shift to us-west2, error rate creeping from 0.3% -> 0.8% during 50% weight. Will stop at any spike >1.5%.
Lena: Keep updates here. If provider can't show progress in 15m, we'll trigger DR full failover and escalate to exec comms. Everyone tag relevant teams in incident page and add logs as they come. :warning:
